T1110.001.description: Adversaries may attempt to guess credentials for existing user accounts by brute forcing authentication interfaces.

T1110.003.description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many accounts.

T1548.003.description: Adversaries may execute commands with elevated sudo privileges or exploit misconfigurations in /etc/sudoers.

T1053.003.description: Adversaries may abuse the cron utility to perform task scheduling for periodic malicious execution.

T1036.description: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate to users or security tools.

T1562.001.description: Adversaries may modify and/or disable security software or collectors to evade detection.

T1071.001.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic to blend in with normal network activity.

T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on hosts across the network.

T1059.004.description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shells such as sh, bash, or zsh to execute various system commands and payload scripts.
